dossier.architecture: Wide four-bar coral intake, compact elevator and separate algae collection.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; precise module specification not established by reviewed interview.
subsystems.intake: Wide four-bar folds inward under frontal impact. Composite plates and roller geometry were iterated; thicker carbon followed week-5 damage.
subsystems.transfer: Ground pickup feeds lightweight two-sided coral/algae end effector.
subsystems.scoring: Two-stage continuous string elevator; low carriage hardware and adjustable bracing reduce mass and top-stage wobble.
subsystems.endgame: Second major climber version adds guide wings, powered cage capture and latches; reported alignment/sequence improved from about 20 to 10 seconds.
subsystems.controls: Two Limelights for piece/pose detection and reef alignment; autonomous detection zones preserve partner compatibility.

versions: Climber version 2 recovers late-match cycling time. Algae floor-to-net use increased once alliances filled reefs faster.
dossier.analysis: The team explicitly identifies serviceability as a weakness: some intake changes took 30–45 minutes. A strategically attractive pickup can still be expensive to maintain, and that cost should be included when borrowing the mechanism.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2025-1678 · Wide pickup, light elevator and faster cage capture solve different delays
context_documents.body:
# 2025-1678: Wide pickup, light elevator and faster cage capture solve different delays

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A wide four-bar collector feeds the lightweight coral/algae effector on a string-driven continuous elevator. The interview describes thicker carbon after a week-five collector member bent and cracked; the caption does not safely establish the thickness. Later cage guides and capture wheels replace a slower alignment approach.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team links width to driver tolerance, elevator construction to speed/weight/CG, and the revised cage capture to reducing an approximately twenty-second climb process toward roughly ten seconds.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The motorized scoring cycle is only one part of match throughput. Wide acquisition can reduce driver correction, while a faster endgame can recover entire scoring cycles. Those gains can justify mass in guides or reinforcement even when they increase subsystem weight. The original and revised climb should not be averaged into one time, and the gain should not be applied to a team whose approach geometry differs.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure failed-pickup rate, full extension deflection and complete cage-approach-to-secured time. Repeat impact tests on the reinforced collector instead of assuming more carbon fixes every load direction.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/gUJUAoHRq8I](https://youtu.be/gUJUAoHRq8I)
